title: Reading signals
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you notice before you hear the words?
A student said that she is not consciously aware of people's body language: if someone crossed their arms she would not pick up that they were closed off.
Another said that he looks at how much they blink and how fast they are speaking, to see whether they are being dishonest or how serious they are.
I said that feeling an emotion is an option, so people can use the option to their advantage, by controlling the feeling or muddling you up in drama.
I said that a very big warning sign is someone who plays a role and does not let you into their family nucleus, because they do not want to be exposed in their true self.
Signals are clues, not proof. Ask a question before you decide what a signal means.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a signal you could learn to notice.
Write what else it might mean.
Write the question you would ask.
Write the role someone plays that you want to understand.

check.q: What did I say an emotion is?
What did a student say he watches?
What did I call a warning sign?
choices: Someone who will not let you into their true self

recap: Notice signals. Do not treat them as proof.
